title: Represent Whole Numbers as Fractions
goal: I can write a whole number as a fraction with denominator one.
catchAll: When each piece is a whole, the denominator is one and the numerator counts the wholes.

teacher.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.

glossary.whole: one complete shape or one 0-to-1 length, as defined in the question
glossary.partition: divide a whole into equal parts
glossary.interval: the distance between neighboring marks on a number line

screens.title: One complete shape is one whole
text: Trace the outside of this strip. It is one whole and has not been cut into smaller pieces.

screens.title: One whole has one whole-size part
text: The highlighted part fills the complete strip.
We can call this 1/1: one complete part out of one part in the whole.

screens.title: Count two wholes
text: Here EACH separate strip is one whole.
The first strip is one whole-size part. The second is another part of that same size.

screens.title: Two over one
text: Both whole strips are selected. Write 2/1.
The top 2 counts the whole strips. The bottom 1 says each counted piece is a complete whole.

screens.title: Keep the whole definition
text: In this lesson, each separate outline is one whole.
Counting two shapes does not divide either shape into two parts. The bottom stays 1.

screens.title: Use one whole unit on a line
text: The length from 0 to 1 is one whole unit.
The point at 1 is one complete jump from zero: 1/1.

screens.title: Keep taking whole-size jumps
text: The point at 3 is three complete unit jumps from zero.
The same point can be labeled 3 or 3/1. Each jump is still a whole, so the bottom remains 1.
